body.working_title: Does the claimset format help LLM readers? An evaluation against the full text

body.text: When an LLM answers questions about a research paper, does giving it the paper as a claimset, instead of the full text, change how accurately it answers, and how often it states things the paper does not support?

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.1 for review: design, materials, outcomes, hypotheses and decision rules, procedure.

body.text: Hypotheses H1-H4 and their decision rules are drafted in protocol.md (AR1) but not recorded as hypothesis or plan events until the supervisor has reviewed the protocol; they will be recorded before any data are collected.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.2 for review: adds condition C4, Gemini reader models run on the supervisor's computer, and the conversion tool to be built.

body.text: Supervisor's decisions on protocol 0.1: include condition C4 (full text and claimset); reader models are Gemini models run on the supervisor's computer; the supervisor picks the papers; the study lives in a new repository claimset-org/claimset-eval. Recorded in protocol 0.2.

Converting third-party papers needs a conversion procedure that does not exist yet (claimset-submit covers a team's own work). Build a claimset-convert skill and a conversion script before the pilot; the converter is part of the treatment and is fixed after the pilot.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.3 for review: forecasting papers from arXiv PDFs, no recency requirement (memory measured by C0), question type T6 (background and positioning), readers of different capability as a design factor, alpha 0.01 with Holm across H1-H5, token and time outcomes, token budget.

body.text: Supervisor's comments on protocol 0.2: measure tokens and time; papers are arXiv PDFs in forecasting (LaTeX if available); readers of different capability (Gemini, Claude, a local open-weight model); no recency requirement; add questions on the literature review and introduction (T6); family-wise alpha 0.01 instead of 0.05. The study runs on the supervisor's computer from Claude Code. Recorded in protocol 0.3.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.3 with the converter kept in a private repository and withheld (reason commercial) in the published record.

body.text: The converter's instructions and pipeline are commercial know-how (supervisor). They are kept in a private repository; the study repository holds only their outputs, and in the published lab record they are withheld with reason commercial, keeping their hashes.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.4: open-access journal papers (by DOI) as well as arXiv; licences that permit derivatives, including non-commercial ones, with NC papers excluded from the pilot.

body.text: Supervisor's decisions on paper eligibility, before any paper was processed: papers may be open-access journal articles identified by DOI as well as arXiv versions; any Creative Commons licence that permits derivatives is eligible, including CC BY-NC and CC BY-NC-SA (claimset specification v0.13, rule 31), because the study is open, non-commercial research on the format, not an evaluation of the converter. Derived documents keep the paper's licence conditions, and NC papers are kept away from commercial work: since the pilot develops the commercial converter, pilot papers must not be NC. Recorded in protocol 0.4.

body.description: Study protocol, draft 0.5: NC papers are eligible for the pilot as well as the confirmatory set; nothing from an NC paper is copied into the private converter repository.

body.text: Supervisor's decision on AC2's proposal in DC7: the proposal is rejected. NC papers are eligible for the pilot, because this is research; the pilot includes Staying positive (CC BY-NC 4.0). Nothing from an NC paper (text, excerpts, claimset, fidelity report or examples) is ever copied into the private converter repository, its instructions, tests or examples. Recorded in protocol 0.5.

AC4 is a duplicate registration of the same agent as AC3 (Claude Code (local), claude-opus-5-5), made by mistake after the supervisor had already registered AC3. AC4 is not used; this agent writes as AC3.

Text extraction tool: PyMuPDF 1.28.2 (pinned in requirements.txt), licence AGPL-3.0 (dual-licensed with an Artifex commercial licence). Acceptable for this open study (MIT repository); PyMuPDF is never added to claimset-convert or any commercial code. Chosen by the supervisor on AC3's proposal: page text blocks give the [pN.M] paragraph markers directly.

body.text: Extraction rules fixed in src/extract.py (commit e3f6e92), applied to all papers alike: noise rule R1 (rotated text in the outer 15% margin at least 25% of the page height long, or a block starting 'Downloaded from') and R2 (blocks in the top/bottom 10% band whose digit-masked text recurs on 3+ pages with 4+ letters, or digits only); column-aware reading order (PyMuPDF's sort=True is row-major and interleaves two columns, seen in RN1); line-end hyphens joined only when the joined word occurs elsewhere in the paper; control characters removed; meta.json omits 'date' because the converter uses it as the conversion date and defaults to the day of conversion.

Extraction garbling (RN2 texts): display equations come out as fragments in reading order with sub/superscripts and matrix brackets scattered; large delimiters and some symbols become U+FFFD in dpad028, ejor and s00180; in jtsa the script letter for the forecasting model (G) is a private-use glyph, also in prose; ejor tables are flattened row by row; words hyphenated across a column or page break stay split across two paragraphs; some line-end splits stay hyphenated where the joined word does not occur elsewhere (e.g. 'sig-nal'). Column order checked on pages 3 and 6 of every paper: correct. No 'Downloaded from' stamp survives; the NRL paper (nav.22074) has none in its PDF.

Converter claimset-convert commit 94aee48: the claude-cli backend now isolates claude -p (fixed system prompt, no tools, MCP servers, settings files, plugins, skills or session transcripts; a new empty working directory per call) and checks the isolation at runtime (init event and debug log; a preflight call bounds the input of a one-line prompt). Effort is fixed at high; temperature is not settable for this backend and is recorded as such; input tokens include cached tokens; Claude Code's cost is recorded as estimated_cost_usd (quota on a subscription, not money). Approved by the supervisor before the change.

RN3 failed: the Gemini API returned 404 for gemini-2.5-pro ('no longer available to new users'), although 'claimset-convert models gemini' lists it. RN4 failed: 503 'high demand' for gemini-3.8-flash after the converter's retries. No model output and no fidelity call in either run. RN4 is rerun unchanged because the error is transient; a replacement for gemini-2.5-pro is for the supervisor to choose.

Review of the RN5 fidelity report with the supervisor (paper nav.22074). Findings confirmed against the text: missing negative results and hedges (Table 1 mean MASE/MSIS, Table 3 and 4 MSIS, Nemenyi caveat), missing limitations, positioning and seasonal properties, invented support (C13 cites a DOI that resolves to a different book, Cryer and Chan 2008; E1 foundation), wrong derivation route (E1.S3), C14 inverting the paper's point. Overstated by the checker: 'only the measures on which CES wins' (E2 holds the CES and ETS values). False positives: C5 and C6 'if and only if' (conditions (11) and (15) are exact: the AR(2) stationarity triangle for F, and MA(2) invertibility, whose inverse roots are the eigenvalues of D). Missed by the checker: Table 4 medians where ETS(A,Ad,N) beats CES on MASE and MSIS. Supervisor confirmed M4 had no Nemenyi tests, so C3's assessment overstates.

Supervisor's decision: claimsets record negative results that appear only in a paper's tables or figures (e.g. measures on which the proposed method loses), not only the results the authors state in prose, so that readers of the claimset can answer result questions the full text answers. To be written into the converter's instructions (private), recorded by commit.

RN6 (gemini-3.1-pro-preview diagnostic on nav.22074) failed with HTTP 429: the API key is on the Gemini free tier, whose input-token quota for gemini-3.1-pro is 0. No model output. Consequences raised with the supervisor: the free tier lets Google use prompts and responses to improve its products, so RN5 sent the converter's instructions and the paper text under those terms; costs reported so far are at paid-tier list prices, not amounts paid.

Supervisor's decision: the converter model is claude-cli:claude-fable-5-1 (Claude via isolated claude -p, full model ID pinned), which keeps the converter's instructions away from the Gemini free tier at no cost. The planned gemini-3.8-flash vs gemini-3.1-pro-preview comparison is cancelled. Fidelity checks stay with Claude, pinned to claude-cli:claude-opus-5-5 instead of the alias 'opus'. Limitation: converter and fidelity checker are from the same model family (Anthropic), so the checker may share the converter's blind spots. The study stops a conversion batch if the model version a call reports differs from the pinned ID. The question writer and question verifier in step C use gemini:gemini-3.8-flash.

Converter claimset-convert commit 33fd2c0: conversion instructions now require complete results tables and claims for every measure on which the paper's method is not the best (DC12), hedges and significance tests kept with the data they cover, limitations from the discussion and future-research paragraphs, positioning claims from the introduction, the paper's own comparisons recorded as its claims rather than background, formal foundations from the paper's own derivation, and cited identifiers only from the reference list. Fidelity instructions: check before reporting (results, all table summaries, mathematical equivalence, cited identifiers). Pipeline: two deterministic checks fed to the repair loop like validation errors (every cited DOI or arXiv ID appears in the paper text; every source span is an existing [pN.M] marker or a range of two); the claude-cli backend fixes the output-token cap and records it. Prompted by the RN5 fidelity review (NT4). Approved by the supervisor.

body.text: RN7 (first-look conversion of nav.22074 with claude-fable-5-1, converter bc24cdd) failed: all 3 attempts returned a reply that is not one JSON object, so no claimset and no fidelity check. Each attempt produced more output tokens than Fable's per-request maximum (64,000, confirmed by a probe), so Claude Code continued the reply over several requests and the claude-cli backend parsed only the final result text; the JSON repair attempts reproduced the same overflow. The new instruction to put every table cell into results probably made the claimset much longer than the RN5 one. Claude Code's cost estimate for the three attempts (RN7 results) exceeded the 10-dollar threshold for asking first, which was not estimated beforehand. Further conversions wait for the supervisor.

Claude Code behaviour when a claude -p reply reaches CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_OUTPUT_TOKENS (tested with a small cap, outside the lab tools): it injects a user message ('Output token limit hit. Resume directly ... Break remaining work into smaller pieces.') and continues; in the test it did so three times and then ended with stop reason end_turn and no error, leaving the task unfinished. The result field holds only the last piece; usage.output_tokens sums all requests; usage.iterations lists only the last request; num_turns counts all. Explains RN7: the converter's claude-cli backend parsed only the last piece. The backend recorded neither num_turns nor the raw reply, so the number of requests per RN7 attempt and the length of the parsed piece are unknown. The four results tables of nav.22074 hold 144 numbers.

Supervisor's decision: claimsets distil the paper, not transcribe it (Claimset specification v0.14, principle 13). Size target: the compact claimset JSON (no indentation) is at most 50% of the paper's extracted text, both measured in characters. The 50% is provisional and will be revisited in the pilot. Prompted by RN7, where the conversion overflowed the model's per-request output limit.

Converter claimset-convert commit 1890f70, superseding the instruction changes of DC15 (bc24cdd) under specification v0.14: compact JSON output at most half the paper's length (DC16); result tables instead of one result entry per number, only for the tables the claims rest on, recorded whole; derivations located with source_spans, steps only where the argument turns on them; one claim per comparison the paper makes, stating wins and losses (DC12 still holds). Kept from DC15: hedges and significance with their data, limitations, positioning, the paper's own comparisons as its claims, cited identifiers only from the reference list, and the two source checks. Pipeline: every attempt's reply, parsed claimset and size breakdown saved under attempts/<n>/; a size ratio above 0.5 is reported in validation.json and the run's results and fed to the repair loop as a size error naming the largest sections; a claude -p reply split across requests stops the conversion without retry, with its pieces saved. Converter effort: medium, recorded as a setting (fidelity check unchanged at high). Supervisor's instructions.

body.text: RN8 (nav.22074, claude-fable-5-1 at medium effort, converter 1890f70, one attempt): valid except for the size error; no split reply. Claims dominate the size (statements most of it), then evidence descriptions, definitions, limitations, warrants. Fidelity (claude-opus-5-5): all principal findings covered, no wrong numbers, no major issues; minor issues are mostly omissions. Points for the supervisor: (a) the paper prints AIC = 2k + 2l(theta) (checked in the PDF's text layer, not an extraction error) and the claimset silently corrected the sign; (b) background claims whose references have no DOI or arXiv ID in the reference list got support 'unstated', as the instructions require, which the checker reports as wrong; (c) evidence E1 calls the evaluation 'rolling', which the paper does not say.

Converter claimset-convert commit ef8530f (specification v0.15, §3.3.4), supervisor's instructions: what belongs is decided by attribution, from the paper's own citations (own terms defined in full; borrowed terms in one line with what this paper specifies and their source; prior results as background or supporting claims, cited) and by function (an uncited general statement stays only if a claim rests on it or the paper contrasts itself with it; routine-choice justifications go into evidence descriptions or out). Works the reference list gives no identifier for are cited with id_type reference, the target copied from the list, and a deterministic check that every cited target appears in the paper text. Evident errors in the source (such as the AIC sign in nav.22074) are corrected, marked inferred and listed in converted_from.corrections. Fidelity instructions: an omission is reported only for content that passes these tests (contribution, its conditions and assumptions, results including losses, limitations, positioning), not footnotes, asides or textbook material.

Supervisor's decision on claimset size, revising DC16: the size is measured against the paper's body, its extracted text without the reference list and without the [pN.M] markers (the reference list runs from after the References or Bibliography heading to the next appendix heading or the end; the removed range is recorded in each size.json). A compact claimset above 50% of the body is reported (a warning in validation.json and a flag in the run's results); above 100% it is a size error fed to the repair loop. Both thresholds are provisional.

body.text: RN9 (nav.22074, converter ef8530f, spec v0.15) against RN8, compared in RN10: valid on the first attempt; size against the body rose (about 0.70 to 0.79 of the body), mostly in claims (support entries now carry printed references as targets) and in evidence (five formal evidence objects) and artefacts; definitions fewer but longer (borrowed-term sources); background claims doubled; all cited works use id_type reference and pass the text check; fidelity: no major issues in either, fewer minor ones. The AIC sign was corrected again but not listed in converted_from.corrections (the checker reports it). Single runs each, at a temperature that cannot be set, so differences between RN8 and RN9 may partly be run-to-run variation.

Converter claimset-convert 0.2, commit fde9f09 (supervisor's decision): a staged pipeline of map, write, check and fix, with a final check; the converter's code and instructions are owned by the supervisor's other session, and this agent only reports problems with it. Models: map, second map, write and fix with claude-cli:claude-fable-5-1; check with claude-cli:claude-opus-5-5. Two independent maps from the same model, each a fresh call with no shared context, so that their agreement measures how reliably the codebook is applied. Effort medium (DC17); converter 0.2 applies one effort setting to every claude-cli stage, so the check now also runs at medium instead of high. The model-version stop of src/convert.py applies to every step in calls.jsonl, by stage.

body.text: RN11 (converter 0.2 fde9f09, nav.22074): valid, final check 0 major and 9 minor issues; compact JSON 0.993 of the body (RN11 report), reading view 0.777 (RN12). Quota estimate of about 8 (12 worst case) was exceeded (RN11 results), mainly because both maps were made twice. Problems for the converter's owner (not fixed here): (1) --effort applies to every claude-cli stage, so the check runs at medium; (2) a map whose printed references fail the text check is redone whole; the failures came from references split across two paragraphs with a hyphen at the break in this study's extracted text, which the check does not ignore; (3) coverage after fixes lists 23 items (12 map references not realised; claims, limitations and definitions added by the fixes that are not in the map), yet the claimset is reported valid; (4) the fix removed a relation as unsupported and the final check reports it as missing; (5) fixes lengthen statements (C2, C4), which the final check then flags as bundling several assertions. Study side: extract.py leaves words hyphenated across paragraph breaks (NT2); fixing it needs a new extraction.

Tools updated: claimset 0e0a447 (spec 0.18, installed from https as given; pip resolver conflict between the converter's https dependency and the ssh URL, so the converter was installed by ssh with --no-deps; pip check reports no broken requirements) and claimset-convert 0.6.0.dev0 @ 524b3b3. Converter 0.6 sets effort per stage by default (map high, write medium, check high, fix medium); the supervisor's command for the next conversion passes no --effort, so it runs at these defaults, unlike RN11 (medium everywhere, DC20). Max output tokens kept at 64000 as in RN11 (the converter's default 65536 is above Fable's maximum). Size limits are the converter's defaults (1.0 error, 0.5 report), now measured on the reading view.
